8 adult dogs don’t have an appropriate form of identification. The licensee is currently using plastic tags affixed to
enclosures to identify adult dogs. There are 5 puppies under 16 weeks of age, without their mother that don’t have any
official form of identification. Official identification is required for each dog at the facility and identification is necessary for
APHIS officials to correctly identify dogs that receive medical treatment, are transported or sold, or otherwise removed
from the facility.
All live adult dogs on the premises, purchased, or otherwise acquired, sold or otherwise disposed of shall be identified by
an official tag affixed to the dog's neck by means of a collar, or shall be identified by a distinctive and legible tattoo
marking approved by the Administration, or by microchip. All dogs less than 16 weeks of age born at the facility must be
identified through use of a microchip, cage card, tattoo, or plastic type collar
To be corrected by 21 Aug 2026

The licensee is not maintaining records of preventative treatments provided to the dogs. The licensee stated that all
routine vaccinations and preventative treatments are given to the animals according to the schedule on the written
program of veterinary care but he is not maintaining records of these treatments. Recording routine treatments of the
medications and vaccines provided to the dogs is important to allow APHIS officials to determine that the dogs are
receiving adequate veterinary care. The licensee must record and maintain medical records that show all treatments and
preventative care given to the dogs at the facility.
To be corrected by 15 July 2026
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with a facility representative.
